subject: Algorithm32 J4 n-order CPU candidate, W27 cumulative scattering through order 4 with pinned-34 incoming recurrence, 48 physical altitude nodes, and view-only actual-altitude interpolation
profileSelection: This Jthrough4 candidate and its numerical identity were fixed before its Kider B1/B2/B3 boundary was generated. These rules copy the already frozen production Default comparator thresholds without tuning.

spectralBoundary.benchmarkProjection: Each native channel value is held constant across its declared 31.333333333333332-nanometer half-open bin [lower, upper), with the final bin closed at 830 nm, and sampled at the unchanged Bruneton 40-point wavelengths. The exact sample-index mapping is min(14, floor(3*k/8)) for k=0..39. No interpolation, source-specific correction, RGB conversion, or fitted scale is applied.
spectralBoundary.reason: This evaluates the Algorithm32 J4 native packet itself on the paper's scoring coordinates without changing the candidate to a 40-channel implementation.

publishedComparatorScale.b2EvidenceQualification: The B2 numeric comparator curves are optional reproductions from the pinned published comparison code because Figure 8 does not publish a numeric table.

rules: Output validity requires all Algorithm32 J4 directional spectral-radiance samples and derived irradiances to be finite and nonnegative, with the complete 17-time by 81-direction boundary present.

B1 is favorable when aggregate RMSE is no greater than the published-model median 18.3 mW m^-2 sr^-1 nm^-1 and all three printed Figure 5 times are no greater than their medians: 17.7 at 10:15, 18.7 at 11:15, and 17.4 at 13:15. B1 is limited when every corresponding value is no greater than the published-model upper quartile: 41.5 aggregate, 39.9, 42.8, and 40.5. It is adverse otherwise.

B2 is favorable when RMSE, absolute bias, and worst absolute residual against the 17-point measured irradiance curve are no greater than the published-source-model medians 12.0182815531215, 11.94158717515906, and 14.100659 W m^-2. It is limited when all three are no greater than the upper-quartile values 20.496807820233318, 20.44040293869519, and 23.056024 W m^-2. It is adverse otherwise.

B3 must reproduce B1's aggregate RMSE within 0.000001 mW m^-2 sr^-1 nm^-1, must retain a complete mismatch map, and reports that same-measurement score beside the paper's published libRadtran values 11.48 coarse and 11.45 refined. B3 inherits B1's classification; it is context rather than a third independent acceptance vote and is not a pointwise libRadtran comparison.

The whole-algorithm benchmark conclusion is favorable when output validity, B1, and B2 are favorable and B3 is consistent and fully mapped; limited when neither B1 nor B2 is adverse, at least one is limited, and B3 is consistent and fully mapped; and adverse when output validity fails, either B1 or B2 is adverse, B3 is inconsistent, or a material mismatch is concealed.

No favorable classification establishes out-of-sample accuracy, flat-geometry accuracy, finite-local-source accuracy, resolved-solar-disc accuracy, or equality with libRadtran. All declared mismatches remain limitations.
